title: Cameron Young Fires Record-Tying 61 to Share Lead at Rocket Classic
excerpt: The world No. 3 birdied seven of his first eight holes on the back nine to vault from the cut line into a three-way tie atop the leaderboard at Detroit Golf Club.
body:
• Cameron Young shot a 9-under 61 in the second round of the Rocket Classic, tying the Detroit Golf Club course record set by Peter Malnati a day earlier.
  • Young climbed from eight shots off the pace to share the 36-hole lead at 10-under with Patrick Cantlay and Patrick Fishburn, with two rounds remaining in the tournament's final edition.
  • The two-time 2026 PGA Tour winner said his putter "went cold" in his second nine — the source of his only frustration on an otherwise dominant day.

Cameron Young erased a sluggish opening round with one of the best performances of the 2026 PGA Tour season, firing a 9-under-par 61 in the second round of the Rocket Classic at Detroit Golf Club on Friday to surge into a share of the lead.

The world No. 3 began the day at 1-under after a modest 69 on Thursday, sitting eight strokes behind first-round leader Peter Malnati. By the time he signed his card, Young had tied Malnati's course record and climbed into a three-way tie at 10-under 130 with Patrick Cantlay and Patrick Fishburn heading into the weekend.

A Blistering Back Nine

Young started on the back nine and wasted no time dismantling the renovated Donald Ross layout. He birdied seven of his first eight holes, including a scorching six-in-a-row stretch from Nos. 12 through 17, to post a back-nine 28 — matching Malnati's front-nine 28 from a day earlier.

https://x.com/GolfChannel/status/2083269483355902461

He narrowly missed an eagle putt on his 13th hole that would have given him sole ownership of the course record. The birdie tap-in brought him to 8-under for the round and level with Malnati at the top.

"It felt like I had a 10-footer for birdie on pretty much every hole. I made a bunch of them in a row on my first nine. Then the putter kind of went cold a little bit for my second nine."

— Cameron Young, after Round 2

That cooling putter was the only blemish Young could point to after tying the course record. He acknowledged some disappointment at not breaking away, adding: "Just really solid golf all the way through. Happy to have kind of played my way back in the tournament a little bit after yesterday."

FedEx Cup Stakes Add Urgency

Young has already won The Players Championship and the Cadillac Championship this season and finished second at The Open Championship. He sits No. 3 in the FedEx Cup points standings with the playoffs two weeks away, seeking to strengthen his position before the postseason begins.

The $10 million purse at Detroit adds financial weight to the weekend. Cantlay, who entered the week at No. 43 in FedEx Cup points, is projected to jump to No. 21 if results hold. Fishburn, a 34-year-old journeyman who has made seven cuts in his last eight starts, could leap from 146th to 61st — potentially locking up a playoffs spot.

One shot behind the leaders sit Rickie Fowler, the 2023 champion of this event, and England's Matt Wallace, who carded a second-round 64. Malnati, Thursday's hero, slipped to 8-under after a 1-over 71 on Friday and is tied for sixth alongside Davis Riley, Xander Schauffele, and five others.

The Tournament's Swan Song

This week marks the eighth and final edition of the Rocket Classic, which debuted in 2019. Detroit Golf Club, which opened in 1899, received a $16.1 million renovation ahead of the event. Young, who finished second here in 2022 and sixth in 2024, called the upgraded course "far more dramatic" and said the added bunkers and expanded greens present a bigger challenge.

"I don't know exactly what's going to happen with the venue, but it's been a great host. If there's a chance to come back in the future, it's certainly somewhere that I would look at coming back."

— Cameron Young

Among those missing the cut at 3-under were defending champion Aldrich Potgieter, U.S. Open champion Wyndham Clark, and India-born Akshay Bhatia, who finished at 1-under.

What's Next

The third round tees off Saturday with Young, Cantlay, and Fishburn in the final group. CBS picks up broadcast coverage from 3 p.m. ET. With 30 players within four shots of the lead on a course yielding low scores by the handful, Moving Day promises fireworks. Young's task: convert a shared lead into outright control — and prove his putter won't go cold when it matters most.
nri_angle: India-born Akshay Bhatia missed the cut at 1-under, while the tournament's final edition closes a chapter for the PGA Tour's Detroit stop.
